title: Your Chance to Buy Shares from Big Owners: Understanding Offer For Sale (OFS)
description: An Offer For Sale (OFS) is when large shareholders, like promoters or the government, sell their existing shares. It's a quick way for them to reduce their st.

faq.q: What is a "floor price" in OFS?
faq.a: The floor price is the minimum price per share at which bids can be placed by investors in an Offer For Sale.

faq.q: Can I sell my OFS shares immediately after allotment?
faq.a: Yes, once the shares are allotted to your Demat account, you can sell them in the secondary market just like any other shares you own.

faq.q: Is there a maximum amount a retail investor can bid in an OFS?
faq.a: Yes, retail investors are typically defined as those bidding for shares with a total value of up to ₹2 lakhs.

faq.q: How is the OFS price for retail investors determined?
faq.a: Retail investors usually receive shares at the "cut-off price" (the price at which most non-retail bids are accepted) with an additional discount applied to it.

faq.q: Who regulates the Offer For Sale process in India?
faq.a: The entire Offer For Sale process, from announcement to allotment, is regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to ensure transparency and protect investor interests.
